object.name: evi.detune~
object.digest: A quirky digital Detune effect, LoFi and old school
object.description: Loosely based on 'mda detune' copyright (c) 1998-2000 Paul Kellett. Includes a linkwitz-riley crossover to shift the focus and strength of the effect. See <o>evi.detune.wrap~</o> for a more complex and expensive version of this algorithm.

inlets.description: Reset of internal detune phase is naive and not anti-aliased.

outlets.description: The phase of the internal modulation in samples, for synchronous downstream processing.

messages.name: history
messages.digest: Top level gen~ [history] / History() declarations can be reset by messages to the object

attributes.name: crossover
attributes.description: Crossover frequency in Hz. Below this crossover point (the bass) the audio is mono summed, saturated and added back into the wet output mix. Above this crossover point the audio is chanelled through the detune effect.

attributes.name: detune
attributes.description: The main detune parameter. 0 = no detune, 1 = maximum detune. The range is 3 semitones and is converted to table lookup position in samples internally.

attributes.name: drywet
attributes.description: The global dry/wet mix of the detuner. 0 is completely dry, 1 is completely wet.

attributes.name: latency
attributes.description: The amount of time in samples used by the detuner. 0=256, 1=512, 2=1024, 3=2048, 4=4096. This has a strong effect of the granular sound of the effect.

attributes.name: mix
attributes.description: Not dry/wet mix. @mix refers to the internal mix of the wet detune chain. It mixes the crossover low/high audio around the feedback path, thus changing the strength of saturated and unsaturated audio into the detuning effect.

attributes.name: smooth
attributes.description: Smoothing time of the internal parameters.

attributes.name: window
attributes.description: The gain window to use in the left/right offset of the up/down detuning. 0=flat, 1=Blackman, 2=Exact Blackman, 3=Blackman-Harris, 4=Hann, 5=Hamming. Default Hann.
